speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse? Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or deformity in your hand or wrist?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis. The history of thumb pain radiating to the wrist, worsening with lifting an infant, and relief with ice is classic for this condition, though your previous fall may have contributed to wrist stiffness. I recommend a specific physical exam (Finkelstein's test) to confirm this before considering imaging.
